checks: For d+2 selected points in one fiber there is a nontrivial affine dependence with coefficients summing to zero, hence both a positive and a negative group. Discarding zero coefficients and normalizing gives two convex representations of one point.

The common point stays in that convex fiber. For every cap, one of the two groups excludes that cap's unique possible exclusive witness. If its color was not selected, either group works. The group's hull is in the closed complement of the open cap, including any points on its boundary.
The common point therefore misses all open caps, contradicting coverage. No full-dimensionality of the fiber, nonvertical normals or strict exclusion from closed caps is used.
